final_text:
**Falcon (FALC), last 6 completed standard sprints (2026.18 to 2026.24), in story points**

| Metric | Average | Range | Std dev |
|---|---|---|---|
| Velocity | 31.8 pts (10.5 items) | 21–40 pts (8–13 items) | 6.5 pts |
| Predictability | 88% | 65–100% | 13 pts |
| Say/do | 79% | 57–94% | 13 pts |

**Per sprint, newest first**

| Sprint | Velocity (pts) | Say/do |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.24 | 34 | 85% |
| 2026.22 | 27 | 66% |
| 2026.21 | 38 | 92% |
| 2026.20 | 21 | 57% |
| 2026.19 | 31 | 80% |
| 2026.18 | 40 | 94% |

2026.23 was left out because it was an IP (innovation and planning) sprint, which isn't comparable.

**What I'd take from it**
- **Velocity is noisy.** The 6-sprint average is about 32 pts, but individual sprints ran from 21 to 40. The average is only a rough planning figure.
- **Say/do averages 79%.** In a typical sprint the team finished about four-fifths of what it committed. Predictability is higher (88%) because finished work added mid-sprint counts toward it, so it flatters the picture a little.
- **The pattern alternates.** Strong sprints (40, 38) have been followed by weak ones (31, 21, 27). The latest sprint, 2026.24, recovered to 34 pts at 85% say/do.

**Suggested commitment for next sprint:** about 28–32 pts. That's roughly the 6-sprint average, or slightly under it. At 79% say/do, a 32-pt commitment would likely deliver about 25–30 pts. Committing near 34 (the last sprint) is reasonable only if capacity looks the same. Anything above 35 has been hit in just 2 of the last 6 sprints, and the team missed its commitment in most sprints where it tried. If next sprint has known absences, lean toward the low end, since 21 pts has happened.

These figures show past output only. I haven't factored in next sprint's capacity, such as leave or holidays, so adjust for that.

final_text:
**I can't give you a graded runway figure for Osprey, and I wouldn't plan the PI from this backlog as it stands.**

**Runway**
- Wayd returned "Not Enough History" for the Runway check, so there is no number in weeks.
- Osprey completed 7 work items in the 90-day window (19 Jul to 16 Oct), and the check needs at least 10.
- I retried with a 180-day lookback, but the response still reported a 90-day window and the same result. I don't know whether the longer lookback was applied, so it didn't help.
- My own back-of-envelope figure is about 33 weeks. That comes from 18 open items at roughly 0.54 completed per week (7 over about 13 weeks). It rests on only 7 completions, so don't treat it as a measurement. It would also exceed Wayd's 26-week "too long" threshold.

**Backlog shape**
The open backlog is 18 items: 6 active and 12 proposed. Everything is in the Mobile workspace and mostly under the MOB-150 "Offline-first mobile app" parent. The estimates add up to 39 story points, but only 13 of the 18 items have one.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Missing Estimate | **Unhealthy**: 5 of 18 (28%). MOB-232, MOB-234, MOB-236, MOB-239, MOB-242 |
| Net Flow | **At Risk**: 1.29 items created per item completed, so the backlog is growing faster than it drains |
| Stale | **At Risk**: 3 of 18 (17%). MOB-237, MOB-241, MOB-244, none touched since 30 Jun |
| No Parent | **At Risk**: 2 of 18 (11%). MOB-234, MOB-244 |
| WIP Load | Healthy: 1.0 active item per member |
| No Project | Healthy: 1 item (MOB-241) |
| Old Proposed, Unassigned Active, Carry-over, Closed Parent | Healthy |
| Aging WIP, Oversized | Not assessed (not enough history) |
| Rank Inversion | Not applicable |

All thresholds were the defaults.

**Other points**
- All 6 active items are assigned to Marcus Hale, even though the team has 6 members. That is probably why WIP Load looks fine.
- MOB-232 and MOB-234 are both active and unestimated. MOB-234 also has no parent.

**Before planning**
1. Estimate the 5 unestimated items.
2. Triage the 3 stale items: re-rank them or drop them.
3. Give MOB-234 and MOB-244 a parent.
4. Re-check runway once Osprey has 10 or more completions in the window.

I can also pull Osprey's sprint metrics (velocity, say/do) for a second read on throughput, since the runway check doesn't have enough completions to work from.
